text:
maria: Heads-up — Hephaestus14b int4 canary is hitting intermittent OOMs under our default defaults (batch=8, max_new_tokens=512). Observed on two machines in us-west1.
ernie: Ugh. Any logs?
maria: Pasted a short excerpt: ```
[E] oom: alloc failed 3145728000
[E] kv_cache: slot_count=2048 free_slots=60
[info] gpu_mem_peak=43.7GB total=48GB```
devon: Looks like fragmentation + high max_new. When max_new is 512 we keep big KV pages around. Also prefetch was on, which increased simultaneous resident allocations.
sasha: Quick mitigation: reduce max_new_tokens default to 256 for the canary, set prefetch=false, and add kv_trim_threshold=0.15. Anyone object? :eyes:
jen: LGTM. Can we also try soft_slot_reserve=0.06 so coldstarts don't spray slots?
infra-bot: deploy requested by sasha to canary pool (pool=hep-canary, commit=heph-int4-v1). ETA ~5m.
maria: Rolling those changes now on two hosts. Config snippet used: ```
serving.runtime.batch_size: 8
serving.runtime.max_new_tokens: 256
serving.runtime.prefetch: false
serving.runtime.kv_trim_threshold: 0.15
serving.runtime.soft_slot_reserve: 0.06
```
devon: Also suggest adding an adaptive max_new override on long prompts: if prompt_len>1500 then cap max_new to 128. Prevents pathological combos.
sasha: Good idea — we can implement a request-time clamp in routing policy. I'll add a quick rule: 
- match: prompt_len >= 1500
  set: max_new_tokens=128
jen: After the change we saw mem_peak drop to ~38.8GB and no OOMs for ~45 minutes. Still watching.
 m aria: (typo) maria: Confirmed — no OOMs on those hosts for the last 1h. Perf tradeoff: p95 latency +10-14% on generation-heavy tails, but throughput stable.
ernie: For metrics/QA: can we run quality eval on int4-v1 with the new default max_new 256 vs previous 512? Need to ensure no regressions where longer generations are common.
sasha: Scheduling eval job (eval-suite: regen-long-context) — results expected in 3 hours.
devon: Long-term: engineering should look at better slab compaction for the allocator; fragmentation is the root cause. For now, conservative defaults + kv-trim and soft reserves are good prophylaxis.
jen: I'll open a short runbook entry in ops-playbooks: "Hephaestus14b int4 onboarding — memory surge mitigations" with the above config and rollback steps.
maria: Thanks all. If the canary stays clean for 6h we do a staged rollout to dedicated pools with the same defaults and a 24h monitor window. :thumbsup:
